3. Medical Disclaimer

Products and information on this site are for general wellness support only. This is not a substitute for professional medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment. Always consult a qualified healthcare provider for medical concerns.

4. Video Consultation

Our optional video consultation is provided by an independent licensed Mexican physician for travel medicine information and wellness guidance. It is not a substitute for your regular physician and does not create a doctor-patient relationship for ongoing care. The physician exercises independent clinical judgment.

5. Delivery

  • Delivery is available in the Los Cabos area (hotels, villas, yachts, marinas)
  • Typical delivery time: 45-60 minutes
  • Delivery times may vary based on location and demand

6. Payment

  • USD pricing displayed
  • Payment methods: WhatsApp coordination (Cash / Card upon delivery)
  • Prices subject to change

7. Cancellation and Refund

See our Refund Policy.

8. Limitation of Liability

CVU Pharmacy is not liable for adverse reactions to any product. Product use is at your own risk. Read all product labels and warnings.

9. Jurisdiction

These terms are governed by the laws of Mexico, Baja California Sur.

10. Contact

Questions about these terms: WhatsApp +52 624 226 1023

title.rendered: Privacy Policy

content.rendered:
CVU Pharmacy Privacy Policy

Last updated: July 13, 2026

CVU Pharmacy (“we”, “us”) respects your privacy. This policy describes how we collect, use, and protect your information.

1. Information We Collect

  • Contact information (name, email, phone) when you place an order or contact us
  • Delivery information (hotel, address, room number)
  • Order and payment information
  • Communication records via WhatsApp Business
  • Analytics data via Google Analytics (anonymized IP)

2. How We Use Your Information

  • Process and deliver your orders
  • Communicate about your order and service updates
  • Improve our website and services
  • Comply with legal obligations

3. Marketing Cookies

This site uses Google Analytics and Google Ads for measurement and marketing. You can opt out via the cookie preferences banner or your browser settings.

4. Data Sharing

We do not sell personal information. We share information only with:

  • Delivery partners to fulfill orders
  • Payment processors (encrypted)
  • Legal authorities when required by law

5. Your Rights

You can request access to, correction of, or deletion of your personal information at any time.

6. Contact

Questions about this policy: contact us via WhatsApp at +52 624 226 1023 or email ramigool20@gmail.com

title.rendered: How to Travel Home with Medication from Mexico — Complete Guide (2026)

content.rendered:
Home  ›  Travel Guide

TRAVEL GUIDE

How to Travel Home with Medication from Mexico

A clear, up-to-date 2026 guide for travelers on bringing pharmacy purchases from Mexico back to the U.S., Canada, and the EU — what is allowed, what needs a OTC, and what to declare.

TL;DR — Key Takeaways

  • Most travelers may bring a personal supply (commonly up to ~90 days for the U.S. & Canada, ~30 days for the EU) of ordinary medication.
  • Keep everything in its original, labeled pharmacy packaging.
  • Declare all medication at customs — honesty is free; failing to declare is not.
  • Over-the-counter items are usually straightforward; OTC-only items should travel with a valid OTC.
  • Controlled or restricted medicines have strict limits — check official CBP, DEA and TSA guidance before you fly.

1. The Legal Basics — How Much Can You Bring?

Every country sets its own rules for personal medication brought across the border, but the shared principle is simple: quantities should reflect personal use, not resale. As a general guideline, the United States and Canada typically allow up to roughly a 90-day personal supply of ordinary medication, while the European Union commonly expects around a 30-day supply. These are guidelines, not guarantees — the final decision always rests with the border officer, and rules vary by medication and airline.

The safest approach is to carry only what one person reasonably needs for a trip plus a modest buffer, and to be ready to explain what each item is and why you have it. When in doubt, contact your destination country’s customs authority before you travel.

Good to know: "Personal supply" is about quantity and intent. Large, wholesale-looking amounts can raise questions even for common medicines.

2. Over-the-Counter vs. OTC

In Mexico, some products are available over the counter (OTC) that may be OTC-only back home — and vice versa. What matters at the border is how your home country classifies the item, not how it was sold in Mexico.

  • OTC items (for example everyday pain relievers, antacids, or antihistamines) are usually the most straightforward to bring back for personal use.
  • OTC-only items should ideally travel with a valid OTC or a doctor’s note, kept alongside the medication in its labeled packaging.

If you are unsure whether something you bought is treated as OTC-only at home, it is worth confirming before you fly.

3. Controlled & Restricted Medicines — Read This Carefully

Some categories of medicine are tightly regulated everywhere. These are often called controlled substances, and they can include certain sleep aids, strong pain treatments, and specific therapies. Rules for these are far stricter: some require special documentation, some have very low personal limits, and some may not be brought across a border at all.

Because the specifics change by country and by product, this guide does not attempt to list individual medicines. Instead, the rule of thumb is: if a medicine is controlled or requires a OTC at home, treat it as requiring a valid OTC and advance research. Always confirm with the official authorities listed below before travelling with anything in this category.

Important: Never attempt to carry a controlled medicine across a border without confirming the rules and carrying proper documentation. Penalties can be serious. When unsure, do not pack it — ask an official source first.

4. Documentation Checklist

Carrying the right paperwork turns a potentially stressful border moment into a quick formality. Before you fly, gather:

  • A valid OTC or doctor's note for any OTC-only medicine.
  • Medication in its original, pharmacy-labeled packaging.
  • The pharmacy receipt or invoice for your purchase.
  • A simple written list of what you are carrying and what each item treats.
  • Your destination country's current customs guidance, saved offline.

5. Packaging & Labeling

How you pack matters. Keep medicines in their original containers with the pharmacy label intact — this shows what the product is, who it is for, and where it was dispensed. Avoid transferring pills into unlabeled daily organizers for the border crossing itself; you can sort them once you are home. Pack medication in your carry-on where possible, so it stays with you and remains within reach if an officer asks about it.

Two more habits: photograph every label, OTC and receipt before you fly, and save daily pill organizers for after you clear customs — sort doses at home, not before the border.

6. Declaring at Customs

When you arrive home, declare your medication if the customs form or officer asks about goods, medicines, or items acquired abroad. Declaring is simple, free, and expected. Have your medication and documentation accessible so you can answer questions calmly. Border officers deal with returning travelers carrying personal medicine every day — a clear explanation and proper labeling is usually all that is needed.

Electronic kiosks and declaration apps count too — answer medication questions exactly as you would with an officer. Unsure whether something needs declaring? Declare it: the question is free, the mistake is not.

7. What NOT to Bring

To avoid trouble, leave behind anything that falls into these buckets:

  • Quantities that look commercial rather than personal.
  • Controlled or restricted medicines without proper documentation and prior confirmation that they are permitted.
  • Medicines with no label, no receipt, and no way to identify them.
  • Anything a friend asked you to carry on their behalf that you cannot personally account for.

8. Country-Specific Rules — U.S., Canada, UK & EU

Most travelers flying home from Los Cabos land in one of four places — each with its own border rules. A practical summary, with primary sources:

United States

U.S. guidance generally allows a personal supply of up to about 90 days of ordinary medication, in original packaging and declared on arrival. Controlled substances face far stricter limits, and some products sold in Mexico may not be permitted at all. CBP officers make the final call — check CBP and DEA guidance before you fly.

Canada

Health Canada allows travellers a single course of treatment or a 90-day supply, whichever is less, in pharmacy-dispensed or original retail packaging. Declare everything on your CBSA declaration; controlled substances follow separate, stricter federal rules — see Travel.gc.ca.

United Kingdom

The UK allows up to a 3-month supply of personal medicine. Controlled drugs must travel in hand luggage with a letter of proof: your name, travel dates, each medicine with dose and strength, and the prescriber’s signature. Some categories need a licence — see GOV.UK.

European Union

There is no single EU-wide allowance — each member state sets its own limits, with a 30-day personal supply a common benchmark for restricted medicines. Within Schengen, controlled medication may require a Schengen certificate. Check the customs authority where you land — and where you connect.

9. Medications That Need Extra Documentation

Some categories attract extra attention at security and customs — officers need proof they are legitimately yours. If anything you carry falls into these groups, allow extra time and keep paperwork within reach:

  • Injectable medicines and syringes (insulin pens, auto-injectors) — carry the pharmacy label and a doctor's note for the needles.
  • Liquid medication over 100 ml / 3.4 oz — permitted when medically necessary, but declare it at the checkpoint.
  • Temperature-sensitive medicines — coolers and gel packs are allowed for medical use; officers may inspect them.
  • Controlled substances such as strong pain treatments or sedative sleep aids — strict limits apply; undocumented transport can be a serious offence.
  • Cannabis-derived products, including CBD — often illegal to carry across borders even where sold legally; verify both countries' rules first.

Ask the dispensing pharmacist how a product is classified, and confirm with the official sources below. Need a doctor’s note before you fly? You can talk to a licensed doctor by video from your hotel.

10. How to Pack Medication for a Long Flight

Carry-on, not checked. Cabin bags stay with you and hold a stable temperature; checked luggage can sit on hot tarmac or go missing. Keep essential medicines and documents in the cabin.

At the checkpoint, solid tablets and capsules screen without limits. Declare medically necessary liquids above 100 ml / 3.4 oz to the officer; you can request a visual inspection instead of X-ray screening.

  • Original labeled packaging, OTC medications and receipts together in one pouch
  • A few days' buffer supply for delays or missed connections
  • An insulated pouch with gel packs for temperature-sensitive items
  • Doses mapped to time-zone changes — ask your doctor how to adjust timing on long routes

Running low before the flight home? Same-day pharmacy delivery in Cabo can bring labeled, receipted products to your hotel before you pack.

11. If Customs Questions Your Medication — What to Do

Even well-prepared travelers get pulled aside occasionally. If an officer questions your medication, make verification easy:

  • Stay calm and answer honestly — inspections of personal medicine are routine.
  • Show your paperwork: OTC or doctor's note, receipt, and labeled packaging.
  • If something is detained, ask for written documentation of what was taken and how to follow up.
  • If the medicine is essential, say so immediately and ask about your options.
  • Foreign visitors can ask their embassy or consulate for help if a situation escalates.

If medication is seized, do not argue at the desk — follow the written process and arrange a replacement through your own doctor. Before you leave Cabo, a house-call doctor can help you get documentation in order.

Important: Never sign documents you do not understand, and never offer payment — ask for a supervisor or consular assistance instead.

12. Frequently Asked Questions

How much medication can I bring back from Mexico?

For personal use, travelers can generally bring up to roughly a 90-day supply for the U.S. and Canada, and about a 30-day supply for the EU. These are guidelines; the officer at the border makes the final call, and limits differ for controlled medicines.

Do I need a OTC to bring medication home?

If the medicine is OTC-only in your home country, you should travel with a valid OTC or doctor's note kept with the labeled packaging. Over-the-counter items for personal use usually do not require one.

Should I declare medication at customs?

Yes. Declaring medication is simple, free, and expected when the form or officer asks. Keep your medication and documentation accessible.

Can I bring controlled medicines back?

Controlled medicines are strictly regulated and sometimes cannot be carried across a border. Always confirm the current rules with official sources such as CBP, DEA and TSA, and carry proper documentation before travelling with anything in this category.

How should I pack my medication for the flight?

Keep everything in its original labeled packaging and pack it in your carry-on where possible, so it stays with you and is easy to show if asked.

Can I mail or ship medication home instead of carrying it?

Usually no — many countries tightly restrict medicine sent by mail, and unauthorized packages can be seized. A documented personal supply in your carry-on is generally the safer route.

What happens if I don't declare medication at customs?

Undeclared medicine can be seized and may bring fines or penalties — even for products that would have been allowed had you declared them. Declaring costs nothing; when in doubt, declare.

Do connecting flights change the rules?

They can. If you clear customs or security in a third country, its rules can apply to what you carry. Check every country on your itinerary, including layovers.

Official Sources

Rules change and vary by medication, quantity, and airline. Always verify with the primary authorities before you travel:

  • U.S. Customs & Border Protection (CBP)
  • U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA)
  • Transportation Security Administration (TSA)
  • Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA)
  • UK Home Office — Take medicine in or out of the UK (GOV.UK)
  • Government of Canada — Travelling with medication
Disclaimer: This article is general information only and is not legal or medical advice. Regulations change frequently. Consult official government sources and a qualified professional for your specific situation before travelling with any medication.

Video Consultation FAQ

Most video consultations take about 10 to 15 minutes. You choose an available time slot and join from your phone, tablet, or laptop - no app or download required.

If the doctor believes you need an in-person exam, they will tell you clearly and recommend next steps. We can also help you arrange a house-call doctor visit to your hotel or villa in Los Cabos.
Do the doctors speak English?
Yes. Consultations are available in English and Spanish, so you can explain your concerns comfortably and understand every recommendation.
How is my personal information protected?
Your video call takes place on a secure, encrypted video platform, and your booking details are handled confidentially. They are used only to arrange your consultation and are never sold or shared for marketing.

<h2>House-call doctor in Cabo — frequently asked</h2>
<p>Quick answers to what most travelers ask before booking a CVU house-call MD.</p>
</div>
<div class="cvu-faq">
<details>
<summary>How fast can a doctor arrive at my hotel in Cabo San Lucas?</summary>
<div class="cvu-faq-body">Most in-suite MD visits in Cabo San Lucas and the central Corridor are with you within 45–75 minutes of confirming on WhatsApp. Outlying zones like Pedregal, Diamante, Puerto Los Cabos and East Cape may take 60–120 minutes depending on traffic and gated-community access. We confirm the exact ETA before you commit.</div>
</details>
<details>
<summary>Are the doctors licensed?</summary>
<div class="cvu-faq-body">Yes. Every CVU doctor is a Mexican physician with a current Cédula Profesional (Mexican federal medical license). Our MDs speak working English with travelers and operate within COFEPRIS-authorized scope.</div>
</details>
<details>
<summary>Can the doctor issue medication orders I can fill in Cabo?</summary>
<div class="cvu-faq-body">Yes. Our MDs issue medication orders on official Mexican letterhead valid at our pharmacy at Plaza Gali and at any licensed pharmacy in Mexico. We can fill the script and deliver it to your hotel room directly, so you don’t need to leave the suite.</div>
</details>
<details>
<summary>Is this a real exam or just a video call?</summary>
<div class="cvu-faq-body">We offer both. Most travelers book an in-suite house-call exam (physical exam, vitals, history). For minor concerns or triage, we also offer a 15-minute video consult on WhatsApp/Zoom — useful for medication resupply or deciding whether a house call is warranted.</div>
</details>
<details>
<summary>How long does a house-call visit take?</summary>
<div class="cvu-faq-body">Most house-call visits run 30–60 minutes from arrival to wrap-up. Telemedicine consults are 15 minutes. Pre-surgery consults and complex cases can run 60–90 minutes if needed.</div>
</details>
<details>
<summary>What does a house-call doctor in Cabo cost?</summary>
<div class="cvu-faq-body">Our menu starts at $79 for a video consult, $200 for a daytime in-suite house call, $295 for an after-hours visit, and up to $249 for a pre-surgery consult — all in USD, all-inclusive of mobile delivery within Cabo, Corridor and San José. Prices subject to change. Lab tests, imaging and IV drips billed separately.</div>
</details>
<details>
<summary>Do you accept insurance?</summary>
<div class="cvu-faq-body">We don’t bill insurance directly. Most U.S. and Canadian travel-medical policies reimburse out-of-pocket house-call care; we provide an itemized invoice in English with our COFEPRIS information so you can submit for reimbursement after your trip.</div>
</details>
<details>
<summary>What if it’s an emergency?</summary>
<div class="cvu-faq-body">We do not provide 911-level emergency care. If you have chest pain, severe shortness of breath, severe bleeding, signs of stroke, severe abdominal pain or any life-threatening symptom, call 911 in Mexico or proceed directly to the nearest hospital. For urgent but non-emergency issues, our 24/7 house-call team can usually get an MD to your suite faster than an ER queue.</div>
</details>

<div class="cvu-trust-icon"><svg viewBox="0 0 24 24"><path d="M12 2C6.48 2 2 6.48 2 12s4.48 10 10 10 10-4.48 10-10S17.52 2 12 2zm-1 15-5-5 1.4-1.4 3.6 3.6 7.6-7.6L20 8l-9 9z"/></svg></div>

<section class="cvu-section">
<div class="cvu-section-inner">
<div class="cvu-section-head">
<span class="cvu-mini-eyebrow">FAQ</span></p>
<h2>Nurse care in Cabo — frequently asked</h2>
<p>Quick answers to what most travelers ask before booking a CVU nurse visit.</p>
</div>
<div class="cvu-faq">
<details>
<summary>How fast can a nurse arrive at my hotel in Cabo San Lucas?</summary>
<div class="cvu-faq-body">Most in-suite RN visits in Cabo San Lucas and the central Corridor are with you within 45–75 minutes of confirming on WhatsApp. Outlying zones like Pedregal, Diamante, Puerto Los Cabos and East Cape may take 60–120 minutes depending on traffic and gated-community access. We confirm the exact ETA before you commit.</div>
</details>
<details>
<summary>Are the nurses licensed?</summary>
<div class="cvu-faq-body">Yes. Every CVU nurse is a registered nurse with current Mexican licensure (Cédula Profesional). Our nurses also speak working English with travelers and follow a brief health-screening protocol before any procedure.</div>
</details>
<details>
<summary>What can a nurse do at my hotel?</summary>
<div class="cvu-faq-body">A nurse can administer IV fluids and vitamins, give intramuscular and subcutaneous injections (B12, Toradol, ondansetron, etc.), clean and re-dress wounds, monitor vitals, manage medications, support post-op recovery, and stay on shift for private nursing. For prescribing or diagnosing, our House-Call Doctor team handles that.</div>
</details>
<details>
<summary>Do I need a medication order for a nurse visit?</summary>
<div class="cvu-faq-body">For a general visit, vitals check or wound care, no medication is needed. For injections of medication medications, we either need the medication order you brought or our House-Call Doctor can write one after a short consult. Sealed supplies are CVU-provided either way.</div>
</details>
<details>
<summary>How long does a nurse visit take?</summary>
<div class="cvu-faq-body">Most visits run 30–90 minutes from arrival to clean-up. An injection visit is usually 20–30 minutes; an IV administration runs 45–75 minutes; wound care is 20–45 minutes; post-op shifts run 4 hours and up.</div>
</details>
<details>
<summary>What does a nurse visit in Cabo cost?</summary>
<div class="cvu-faq-body">Our menu runs from $89 for an injection visit to $599+ per day for a 24/7 private nurse shift, in USD and all-inclusive of mobile in-suite delivery within Cabo San Lucas, San José del Cabo and the Corridor. Outlying gated/yacht areas may carry a small travel fee, always confirmed on WhatsApp before dispatch. Prices subject to change.</div>
</details>
<details>
<summary>Do you accept insurance?</summary>
<div class="cvu-faq-body">We don’t bill insurance directly. Most U.S. and Canadian travel-medical policies reimburse nurse care as out-of-pocket care; we provide an itemized invoice in English with our COFEPRIS information so you can submit for reimbursement after your trip.</div>
</details>
<details>
<summary>Can a nurse stay for a full shift in my villa?</summary>
<div class="cvu-faq-body">Yes. We arrange 8h, 12h or full 24h private RN shifts for villas, yachts and hotel suites — common for post-op recovery, elderly travelers and high-needs care plans. Shift rates start at $599 USD per day and we confirm scope on WhatsApp before dispatch.</div>
</details>
</div>
</div>

					<div class="vc-faq vc-anim"><details><summary>Do I need a doctor’s order for IV therapy?</summary><div class="a">No special paperwork is needed for our wellness IV drips. After your consultation, a licensed nurse typically arrives at your hotel, villa, or yacht within 60–90 minutes — same-day across most of Los Cabos.</div></details><details><summary>Is IV therapy safe?</summary><div class="a">Our drips are administered by licensed nurses using sterile, single-use, medical-grade supplies, after a physician screening. Your nurse stays with you and monitors the entire session. As with any medical procedure there can be minor risks — that is exactly why we screen first.</div></details><details><summary>Can I get an IV at my hotel, villa, or yacht?</summary><div class="a">Yes. We serve hotels, private villas, yachts and marinas across Cabo San Lucas, the Tourist Corridor, and San José del Cabo. Wellness IV drips range from $165 to $395 USD depending on the formula and add-ons. The exact price is confirmed before you book — no hidden fees. We accept credit cards, USD cash, and wire transfer.</div></details><details><summary>What if I feel unwell during the IV?</summary><div class="a">Tell your nurse — they remain by your side for the entire session and can slow, pause, or stop the drip at any time. Our physician is on call throughout. For any emergency, call 911 immediately.</div></details><details><summary>Do you take insurance?</summary><div class="a">We do not bill insurance directly. Once the physician confirms your drip, a licensed nurse is dispatched to your location — usually the same day.</div></details><details><summary>Is the consultation really free?</summary><div class="a">Yes. The video consultation with our licensed physician is included at no extra cost with every IV therapy booking and every pharmacy delivery order — a $150 value. The physician confirms the drip is appropriate for you; there is never a separate consultation charge.</div></details><details><summary>Can I pay in USD?</summary><div class="a">Yes. Every price is quoted in USD up front on WhatsApp before we dispatch. Pay by credit or debit card, Apple Pay, or cash (USD or MXN) when your nurse arrives — with an itemized receipt in English.</div></details><details><summary>How is IV therapy different from drinking water?</summary><div class="a">IV drips deliver fluids, electrolytes, and vitamins directly into your bloodstream rather than through digestion, and a licensed nurse tailors the session to you. Whether an IV or simple oral hydration makes more sense for your situation is exactly what the free physician consultation is for.</div></details><details><summary>Can I combine IV therapy with pharmacy delivery?</summary><div class="a">Absolutely. Your nurse can bring vitamins, supplements, sunscreen, and personal-care items along with your drip — and any pharmacy order also includes the free doctor consultation. Riu Santa Fe is busy, social, and a regular pharmacy delivery stop for our team. Our drivers know the front desk procedure and deliveries are typically handed off there for guest pickup. We also accept WhatsApp orders straight from the room.

Riu guests are heavy on hangover recovery kits, sunscreen, ibuprofen, electrolytes, and medications for traveler stomach issues. We also handle medication resupply, plan B, and basic first aid for the occasional pool tumble.

  • Pain relievers, allergy and cold medicine
  • Stomach remedies and electrolytes
  • Sunscreen, after-sun, and reef-safe options
  • Baby and pediatric supplies
  • Vitamins, supplements, and wellness items

How to Order

WhatsApp is the fastest way to reach us. Send a message with what you need and your room or villa number at Riu Santa Fe, and we will confirm price and an honest ETA. Most orders are at your door in under an hour. We accept USD, MXN, and most major cards.

Need a pharmacy at Riu Santa Fe right now?
